mike.s: Hey team — suddenly getting 401 invalid_api_key from /v1/generate. No code changes on our side, just CI redeploy. Example curl: 

mike.s: ```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: ApiKey=my_super_secret_key_abc123" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

maria_support: Thanks, mike. Quick Qs: is that the exact header you use from your app stack or did you hand-edit the curl? Also can you confirm the key you're sending is the active key in the dashboard (not a rotated/old key)? :mag_right:

mike.s: That's copied from our deployment template (we inject from AWS Secrets Manager). I checked dashboard — key is listed as active and last used earlier today. No rotation events in the logs.

maria_support: Ok. One thing I noticed — your curl shows `Authorization: ApiKey=...` (with an equals sign). Redwood accepts the key in `Authorization: Api-Key <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>` (no trailing `=` or `key=`). Can you paste the exact raw HTTP header that reaches your backend? Sometimes templating adds `ApiKey=` when concatenating strings.

mike.s: Hmm, in our app code we use python requests and we do: 

mike.s: ```py
import requests
auth = (os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), '')
resp = requests.post(url, auth=auth, json=payload)
```

maria_support: Aha. That will send Basic auth (Authorization: Basic <base64>) not the Api-Key header. The `auth=(user,pass)` tuple in requests triggers HTTP Basic Auth. That would explain a 401 invalid_api_key because Redwood sees Basic auth and not ApiKey header.

mike.s: Oh wow. That was a stupid copy/paste from an internal helper. We assumed requests would put the first value in Authorization raw.

todd_oncall: Yep — easy trap. Two options: set the header explicitly or use a custom auth object. Example fix: 

todd_oncall: ```py
import os, requests
headers = { 'Authorization': f'ApiKey {os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")}' }
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
```

maria_support: Alternatively if you want Bearer style: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` also works. After you deploy that change, send a curl-equivalent and we can confirm.

mike.s: Pushed the header change to staging, re-deployed. Doing a quick test now...

ci-bot: deploy mike-service/staging #42 succeeded in 38s by mike.s

mike.s: Ok retest: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: ApiKey my_super_secret_key_abc123" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

maria_support: Received your request — shows successful 200 proxied from our ingest. Looks good on our side. :white_check_mark:

mike.s: Nice, that fixed it. Can we add a note to our repo to avoid using `auth=(key, '')`?

maria_support: Good idea. I'll drop a short snippet in the thread that your team can paste into the README. Also flagging the support ticket as resolved. If you hit anything else, ping me directly.

mike.s: Thanks everyone! :pray:

maria_support: Closing out — root cause: used requests Basic Auth tuple which produced `Authorization: Basic ...` instead of the expected `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`. Resolution: set header explicitly or use `Bearer` style.
